question: A 54-year-old woman is brought to the emergency department by a nurse 30 minutes after receiving scheduled radiation therapy for papillary thyroid cancer. After the radioisotope was ingested, the physician realized that a much larger fixed dose was given instead of the appropriate dose based on radiation dosimetry. Which of the following pharmacotherapies should be administered immediately to prevent complications from this exposure?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Excessive radiation exposure" -> "Thyroid gland damage" -> "Release of high levels of thyroid hormones" -> "Increased risk of thyroid storm" -> "Potassium iodide administration to block thyroid hormone synthesis" -> 95% CHAIN: "Excessive radiation exposure" -> "Increased risk of developing thyroid cancer" -> "Potassium iodide administration to reduce the risk of radiation-induced thyroid cancer" -> 95%
analysis: In this scenario of accidental radiation exposure in a patient with papillary thyroid cancer, the immediate administration of potassium iodide is crucial. Potassium iodide can help protect the thyroid gland from absorbing radioactive iodine, reducing the risk of radiation-induced thyroid damage.
